title: A Classical Sequential Growth Dynamics for Causal Sets
version: arXiv:gr-qc/9904062v3 (revised 26 Jun 2004; SU-GP-99/4-1); Phys. Rev. D 61, 024002 (2000); doi 10.1103/PhysRevD.61.024002. Text from ar5iv render; key formulas cross-checked against the v3 LaTeX source (e-print dated 2004-06-26).
section_locator: Sec. 1.1 (natural labeling, fictitious external time); Sec. 3 (internal temporality, discrete general covariance, Bell causality Eq. (2), Markov sum rule); Sec. 4 (Lemmas 1-4, Eqs. (3)-(13), Claims on inequalities); Sec. 4.4 (verification, Eqs. (14)-(15)); Sec. 5 (Eqs. (17)-(18), Prob_N(C)=W(C)P(C)); Sec. 7 (open questions); Appendix Lemmas 5-6. The paper has no numbered theorem; the main result is the derivation in Sec. 4.
assumptions: Markov transition probabilities; internal temporality (births to the future of or unrelated to existing elements; natural labelling); discrete general covariance (path independence of the product of transition probabilities); Bell causality (ratio of sibling transition probabilities depends only on the union of precursor sets); Markov sum rule; genericity: no transition probability vanishes (Sec. 4); elements counted as distinguishable (sum-rule multiplicities).
conclusion: Authors' derivation: under those conditions the transition probability is alpha_n = lambda(w,m)/lambda(n,0) with lambda(w,m)=sum_{k=m}^{w} C(w-m,w-k) t_k, free parameters t_n>=0, t_0=1 (equivalently q_n with q_n^-1 = sum C(n,k) t_k); transitive percolation is t_n=t^n. Label-independent formation weight P(C)=prod_x lambda(w(x),m(x))/prod_j lambda(j,0). Authors state that labels are fictitious/gauge and that statements such as 'when the causet had 8 elements it was a chain' are meaningless; they describe the phenomenological passage of time as a manifestation of growth. These are the authors' interpretive claims, not consequences of the mathematics.
proof_status: Hand derivation in the paper (Lemmas 1-6 with proofs); no formal or machine verification. Not independently re-derived here beyond reading; the n<=5 finite check in knowledge/defeat-search/csg_ancillarity_check.py (coordinator) is exact rational arithmetic for two parameter vectors through n=5, not a general proof or an observer model. Coordinator re-ran it on 2026-10-19.
dependencies: Markovian sequential growth; Kleitman-Rothschild entropy problem motivation; Sorkin quantum measure (gr-qc/9401003) for the quantum extension, not used
open_questions: Can Bell causality be formulated without a birth sequence? (Sec. 7, authors)
Are all meaningful assertions combinations of partial-stem occurrence? (conjecture, Sec. 5/7, authors)
Non-generic cases with vanishing transition probabilities (originary models) left open by the authors
Equation numbers are those of the ar5iv/LaTeXML v3 render; the journal numbering was not checked.
relevance: Anchor for growth-model comparison (candidate A): defines the label-independence and Bell-causality conditions and the transition probabilities.
limits: Classical model family; no observers, records or clock construction in the paper; passage language is interpretive. Text extraction flattens sub/superscripts, so formulas were verified against LaTeX for (6),(7),(12),(17) and P(C_n)=W p^L q^(C(n,2)-R).

title: What becomes of a causal set
version: arXiv:1502.00018v1 (30 Jan 2015); 'forthcoming in the British Journal for the Philosophy of Science' per arXiv comments (publication details not checked). Text from ar5iv render.
section_locator: Sec. 3 'Facing the same dilemma?' (Stein's theorem, counterexample causet R, non-Hegelian subsets); Sec. 4 'Taking growth seriously' (CSG as tenseless history space, localized becoming, label time, gauge-invariant growth, posts, Fig. 3); Sec. 5 conclusion. No numbered theorems.
assumptions: Causet = locally finite partial order (reflexive convention); Stein-style becoming as a binary relation R 'definite as of' that is reflexive, non-trivial, non-universal, automorphism-invariant; CSG dynamics with discrete general covariance; the quotient-by-relabelling measure of Brightwell et al. 2003; identity conditions of events (for coherence of the 'exotic' becoming).
conclusion: Authors' claims: (i) the analogue of Stein's theorem is false in CST (counterexample causet with b,c spacelike related; R includes <b,c> and <c,b> without collapsing to universal); (ii) they suspect large/many non-Hegelian subsets are scarce, but acknowledge little published analytic or numerical evidence, and the no-macroscopic-present conclusion is conditional on that suspicion being right; (iii) they infer Lorentz violation for the highly regular structures at issue, not for arbitrary non-Hegelian subsets; (iv) CSG is compatible with a tenseless history-space reading; (v) localized/observer-dependent becoming is available but has Minkowski analogues; (vi) a novel global, objective but ontologically indeterminate “becoming” (cardinality grows, which elements exist at a stage is not determinate) is compatible with CST, at radical metaphysical cost (vague existence, indeterminate past). Authors do not claim this proposal is physically established.
proof_status: Informal philosophical argument with one explicit counterexample (checkable by hand); no formal proof. The population scarcity statement is the authors' suspicion/inference, not an established genericity result; their cited Meyer estimate is unpublished and unread. The targeted v1 text audit and this attribution correction are recorded in knowledge/audits/fulltext-spotcheck/physics/findings.jsonl, source_id cs-wuthrich-callender-2015-v1. The prior lane snapshot remains in research/redteam/source-repairs/before-records.jsonl (knowledge/causal-sets/sources.jsonl line 2).
dependencies: Huggett 2014, Pooley 2013, Earman 2008, Arageorgis 2012, Dowker 2014 as cited, all unread
open_questions: Whether the cardinality-only 'becoming' is coherent depends on event identity conditions (authors)
Whether the measure being defined only on Omega(infinity) makes the infinite end state prior to the growth (authors raise it)
Whether non-Hegelian-subset statistics hold for realistic causets (only Meyer's unpublished 1+1 estimate cited)
relevance: Closest philosophical prior art for candidate A and for claims that causal-set growth supplies objective passage. The explicit finite counterexample is directly supported; the population-level genericity/Lorentz-inference argument is qualified and conditional.
limits: Philosophy-of-physics argument; the Stein-analogue statement is in prose (Sec. 3), not a theorem with proof. The paper's Stein statement is paraphrased from Stein 1991 and was not checked against it. Coordinator directly checked Secs. 3-4 in the versioned HTML; the prose Stein reconstruction must not be reused as a validated primary theorem (transitivity/strict-versus-reflexive qualifications unresolved). The authors state there is little relevant analytic/numerical evidence and cite an unpublished Meyer estimate; scarcity is not independently established.

title: On the Uniqueness of Embeddings of Causal Sets
version: arXiv:2607.05840v1 [gr-qc], submitted 7 Jul 2026, 39 pages, MSC 83C27, 53C50. Unrefereed single-author preprint. Text from arxiv.org/html v1.
section_locator: Def. 2.6 (well-conditioned embedding, F1-F3, Eqs. (1)-(5)); Lemma 4.1; Lemma 4.3 (covariance matrix isotropy, Eq. (22)-(25)); Prop. 4.16; Thm 4.18 (Eq. (39)); Thm 5.1 (Eq. (40)); Cor. 5.6 (Eq. (48)); Sec. 6.1-6.2 (relation to Malament, Muller). Statements read in full; proofs of Props 4.8-4.15, 5.3 and Appendices A-E were skimmed or not read.
assumptions: Finite causal set; globally hyperbolic Lorentzian manifolds of dimension d with finite volume and curvature scale lambda; density rho with rho*lambda^d >= c_*^(-2d) (log rho V)^2; (F1) exact order preservation, (F2) scale-dependent uniform density, (F3) longest-chain distance preservation (author notes F3's independence from F1-F2 is open); Poisson sprinkling for Part II.
conclusion: Author's claims: two well-conditioned embeddings of one causal set force an epsilon-approximate isometry of the deep interiors, Phi*g2 = g1 + E with ||E|| = O(rho^(-2/(5d)) lambda^(-2/5) log^(3/2)(rho V)); Poisson sprinklings are well-conditioned with probability >= 1-(rho V)^(-K'). Concerns spacetime reconstruction from a completed causal set; it says nothing about growth, becoming or observers.
proof_status: Hand proof in the paper; no formal verification; unrefereed. Only the statements and proof roadmaps were checked here; proofs not audited. The Corollary 5.6 error exponent is the author's, with a footnote that log exponent 3/2 is an upper bound.
dependencies: Bollobas-Brightwell 1992 height of random partial orders
open_questions: Applies to Poisson sprinklings at high density only; non-sprinkled or sparse causets unaddressed
Independent refereeing or reproduction not found
relevance: Anchor for the order-to-geometry reconstruction side of the lane: what fixes a manifold from a completed causet.
limits: A completed-order result. Using it as support for either temporal ontology would require a bridge premise it does not supply. Naming collision: 'covariance' here is the covariance matrix Sigma(x) of embedded points, unrelated to discrete general covariance. Coordinator directly checked Def. 2.6 Eq. (4): delta_D=K_d*sqrt(log(rho*V_M)/(rho*Vol_g(D))), and the statements of Thm. 4.18 and Cor. 5.6 in the v1 HTML on 2026-10-19. This is a statement-level spot-check, not a proof audit.
